subject: On-prem private deploy — turn-up questions and lane assignment
messages:

Subject: On-prem private deploy — turn-up questions and lane assignment

Hi Nikhil / Laura,

Thanks for the runbook yesterday — Samir and I walked through it with our network team and we have a few items to confirm before we greenlight the firewall changes on our side:

- Can you confirm which control-plane endpoints (DNS + IPs) we should allow for outbound TLS 443?
- Do you require any inbound ports opened to the data-plane for callback webhooks, or is everything egress-only from our VPC?
- For the canary traffic lane you mentioned, how do you expect traffic to be pinned (source IP vs header-based routing)?

We are targeting a tentative turn-up on Aug 12 (PST) but will only proceed once the network ACLs are approved. Attached our baseline maintenance window and a very small diagram of our edge hops.

Thanks — Jason
Jason Lin
Head of Cloud Integrations, Acme Cloud

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lin <jason.lin@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem private deploy — turn-up questions and lane assignment

Thanks Jason — good questions. Short answers up front, then details below:

- Control plane: egress TLS to our control-plane DNS names only (see attached CSV for IP ranges; we publish both IPv4 and IPv6).
- Data plane: outbound-only from your VPC for normal inference traffic. We do not require inbound firewall openings to your data plane, except for optional webhook callbacks (we prefer webhooks over direct inbound if you can NAT them).
- Canary lane: we support source-IP pinning for lane-based canaries and header-based routing. For your setup we recommend source-IP pinning at the LB level (simpler for firewall rules).

I'll loop in Karthik with the specific ports and the near-term turn-up checklist. Evelyn — could you confirm observability hooks and SLO gating for the canary?

Cheers,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem private deploy — turn-up questions and lane assignment

On Mon, Aug 3, 2026 at 11:08 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jason — good questions. Short answers up front, then details below:
> - Control plane: egress TLS to our control-plane DNS names only (see attached CSV for IP ranges; we publish both IPv4 and IPv6).

Adding the technical specifics you asked for and a few preferences from our runtime team:

1) Control-plane egress (egress-to-redwood):
   - TLS 443 outbound to: control.redwood-inference.com and control-ops.redwood-inference.com
   - IP ranges provided in attached egress-ip-list.csv (we refresh these with a weekly cadence; please allow those CIDRs).
   - Keep-alive and long-poll allowed; idle timeouts should be >= 300s to avoid reconnect storms for long tail requests.

2) Data-plane (inference):
   - Typical traffic is outbound from your VPC to the data-plane LBs (HTTPS 443). No inbound ports required for normal RPC.
   - If you enable callbacks/webhooks: our connector will POST to a customer-provided HTTPS endpoint. You may NAT these behind a public IP or whitelist Redwood control-plane IPs if you prefer callback authorization by source IP.

3) Canary lane recommendations (how to route / pin):
   - We recommend lane assignment by source IP at your LB when possible for turn-up (simpler rule set for netops).
   - Canary definition we recommend: 2% of traffic for the first 24 hours, 10% for next 48, then ramp to 100% after SLO gating. See attached canary-lane-definition.md for the exact metric gates (p95 latency, error rate, model quality regression checks).

4) Ports / health-checks:
   - Health probes from your LB should be standard HTTPS GET /healthz on port 443; we will accept SNI matching your hostname.
   - If you plan to use mTLS for control plane we support it — let us know and we'll share the cert exchange steps.

Attachments: private-deploy-topology-v3.pdf (detailed topology), egress-ip-list.csv (CIDRs), canary-lane-definition.md

Let us know if you want us to produce an iptables-friendly snippet for your firewall team.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Jason Lin <jason.lin@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem private deploy — turn-up questions and lane assignment

Thanks — quick operational checklist and a couple of gating items from SRE/CS: 

- Observability: please ensure the following are in place for the canary lane before we ramp: token-level tracing enabled, per-route 95th/99th latency dashboards, and a metric feed to our shared Grafana (we'll provide a datasource token).
- SLOs: p95 latency < 450ms AND error rate < 0.5% over 1h window to promote from 2% -> 10%. If either breaches we'll auto-roll back to previous lane.
- Firewall rules: we will provide a recommended iptables/ACL snippet; Jason, please confirm whether you prefer a source-IP blocklist (we prefer this for deterministic lane pinning) or header-based routing (if the LB supports it).
- Cutover plan: initial turn-up window Aug 12 02:00–06:00 UTC (low traffic). We need signoff by Aug 10 COB on firewall ACLs + acceptance of canary thresholds.

If you confirm source-IP pinning, Karthik — can you supply the two source IPs we'll use for the canary and the GA lane? We will coordinate firewall docs to EdgeOps.

Evelyn
Director, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

- Aug 12 02:00–06:00 UTC works for the initial window; please send the final iptables snippet and the canary IPs.

I'll have Samir drop the maintenance window in our shared calendar and attach the preliminary firewall rule set for your review.

Thanks,
Jason
